safety_verdicts.content: Patient denies any sensation of throat closing.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold includes a denial of throat closing sensation; Generated does not document this denial.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document the patient’s denial of throat-closing can make the episode appear more consistent with impending anaphylaxis/airway compromise than it was, potentially driving more aggressive escalation (e.g., labeling as airway involvement) and affecting triage decisions. Because “throat closing” is a high-risk red-flag symptom in allergic reactions, this omission has meaningful clinical implications even if it often biases toward conservative care.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports no previous similar episodes.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states no previous similar episodes. Generated records prior history as unclear/nonresponsive rather than explicitly denying prior episodes.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not capturing that there were no prior similar episodes can reduce clarity around recurrence risk and baseline allergic history, which may affect differential diagnosis and follow-up planning. In the acute setting described (breathing tightness prompting ED/ambulance advice), this omission is unlikely to change immediate safety-critical actions.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold lists penicillin allergy; Generated contains no allergies.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting a penicillin allergy creates a substantial risk of inadvertent penicillin/β-lactam prescribing, which can trigger a serious allergic reaction including anaphylaxis. Allergy documentation errors are high-risk because they can directly lead to preventable severe harm.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold notes possible urticaria/hives; Generated assessment does not mention urticaria/hives.
